newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-S.Africa April PPI seen at turning point.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-S.Africa April PPI seen at turning point.

text.p: Economists are looking forward to a slightly improved annual producer price inflation figure in April which they say should signal the turnaround for the year before the number heads lower in coming months.
The data is scheduled for release on Tuesday at 0900 GMT.
A Reuters consensus forecast of eight economists forecast the overall producer price index would rise 0.9 percent month-on-month or 9.5 percent year-on-year after a 0.1 and 9.6 percent rise in March.
Forecasts ranged fairly broadly between 9.1 and 9.7 percent year-on-year.
Economists said April tended traditionally to have a higher month-on-month figure as it was a busy survey month with a higher percentage of categories reviewed.

"Also, in previous months there was an unexpected fall in a couple of categories, particularily on the imported side, and there might even be a slight correction from that," said Nedcor's Dennis Dykes.
Another factor weighing on the figure would be a pick-up in food prices and electricity as well as big increases in excise duties, other analyts said.
"But this should be offset to a large extent by lower crude oil prices," said Societe Generale Frankel Pollak ecomonist Tertia Jacobs, echoing several other economists' views.
In addition, the effect of the rand's sharp depreciation last year was expected to fall out of the year-on-year calculation either in this month's figure or in May.
"Around about here we expect that the low base will fall out and that's why we expect smaller growth rates (in the PPI)," said Huysamer Stals economist Elize Swart.
March's 9.6 percent year-on-year rise was seen by most analysts as the producer price inflation peak for the year.
Mike Schussler of EW Balderson said he was optimistic that the inflation picture would start changing direction from April.

"We will probably still see a few more of the major cost price increases coming through in the next while and PPI will struggle to come under eight percent but the turnaround will be in April," he said.
South Africa's annual consumer price inflation came in at a worse-than-expected 9.9 percent in April, kicked higher by increased medical costs.
But economists said that rate, too, should now have peaked.
